source: Personal colorectal cancer risk: SEER age-specific rates plus meta-analysis relative risks; colonoscopy effect from NordICC

baseline.source: SEER Cancer Statistics Review 1975-2017, Table 6.10 (colon and rectum, all races, age-specific rates 2013-2017, per 100,000)

family_history.label: a parent, brother, sister or child had colorectal cancer
family_history.source: Roos et al., Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2019;17:2657 (one first-degree relative, case-control studies; cohort studies 1.37)

ever_smoked.label: ever smoked
ever_smoked.source: Botteri et al., JAMA 2008;300:2765 (ever vs never smokers, 26 studies)

obese.label: BMI 30 or higher
obese.source: Ma et al., PLoS One 2013;8:e53916 (obese vs normal BMI, prospective studies)

colonoscopy.source: NordICC, Bretthauer et al., NEJM 2022;387:1547 (ages 55-64, 10 years), as summarized by ACG Evidence-Based GI

sigmoidoscopy.source: Juul et al., Ann Intern Med 2022;175:1525-1533 (4 randomized trials, 274,952 people aged 55-64, 15 years)

fobt.source: Shaukat et al., Long-Term Mortality after Screening for Colorectal Cancer, NEJM 2013;369:1106-1114 (Minnesota trial, 46,551 people aged 50-80, 30 years)
fobt.fit_note: Today most clinics use FIT, a newer stool test that finds more cancers. FIT has no finished randomized trial yet; a study of 5.4 million people found about 10% fewer colorectal cancer deaths after 6 years (USPSTF 2021).
fobt.verified_against: PubMed abstract and NCI CDAS trial summary
